topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series and outlines the specific learning objectives regarding cancer causation and environmental carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Intrinsic versus environmental drivers of cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: They explore how genetic, environmental, and stochastic factors interact to determine overall cancer risk and drive observed geographic variations in incidence.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how infectious pathogens and co-infections contribute to cancer development through cell cycle disruption and chronic immune stimulation.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the molecular mechanisms by which chemical and physical mutagens undergo metabolic activation and produce direct or indirect DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, two-stage carcinogenesis, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how non-mutagenic tumour promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental timing interact with mutagenic initiators to facilitate cancer outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and evaluating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect, test, and assess carcinogenic risks.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: It provides concluding framing that summarizes the lecture's core themes on environmental cancer causes and risk assessment.
